recipes.name: Ham Cake-ettes
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup vegetable oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Mix together mashed potatoes, ham, green onions, 1/4 cup bread crumbs, egg, Dijon mustard, dill weed, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. If mixture is too moist to hold together, mix in an additional 1/4 cup bread crumbs.
Place remaining bread crumbs into a shallow bowl.
Scoop about 1/3 cup of the mixture and form into a ball; slightly flatten into a patty. Press both sides of patty into bread crumbs; tap off any loose crumbs. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat until very hot. Fry patties, 2 to 3 at a time, in hot oil until golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham Cake-ettes
raw_recipe.description: These ham cakes feature mashed potatoes, green onion, and Dijon mustard rolled in panko bread crumbs and fried until golden brown for tasty cake-ettes.

review.reviewBody: I actually ran the ham and the green onions together through my food processor to get the fine consistancy that I was looking for. I actually fried these in my cast iron skillet in a mixture of EVOO and butter. I did not try these myself but my husband and kids thought they were MONEY. NO leftovers. I think these would be excellent for breakfast as a substitute for hashbrowns with a side of sunny side up eggs and bacon. This recipe is SUCH a keeper--thumbs up from my family.

After reading other reviews, I knew I was going to have to add additional seasonings. I doubled the amount of dill, added about 50% more mustard and included 1 tablespoon of powdered Ranch dressing mix. This gave the potatoes substantially more flavor. As noted in other reviews, I also experienced my patties falling apart, so I took the ⅓ cup and divided it into thirds (making each smaller patty about 2 tbsp) and served three as one serving. This made for a much smaller mess and the patties were easier to manage. I also tried air frying and baking some of the patties. Though the air fried patties weren't as pretty (they lacked the color) as the pan fried they were an acceptable alternative to the oil. I would not recommend baking them, they do not get crunchy at all.

Just tried this recipe three times with left over flavor-packed buttermilk garlic mashed potatoes from last night's dinner. The first time I substituted finely chopped onion for the scallions and learned that the potato mixture definitely needs additional panko. The second time I removed the dried dill, because I thought it clashed and suggested there would be a seafood ingredient in the mix (think crab cake.) Third time was the charm; I did a quick pan-fry with the ham and onions before adding to the dill-free potato mixture. The flavor of the onion and ham were fantastic and added much needed golden color to the insides of the potato cakes.

Not sure if I did something wrong, being that so many other people had such great results. I followed the recipe exactly, but I used CountryCrock garlic mashed potatoes from the refrigerated section of the grocery store. They came out so mushy that they fell apart in the frying pan, and made such a mess. I think I will try these again, only with homemade leftover mashed potatoes.

This was fantastic. I doubled the recipe and got 10 patties and had to fight so that I could even get one. Everyone in my family loved it. The girls and I had a fried egg on top and it was extra good. Highly recommended.
I cooked some chopped white onion in butter before adding to the mixture and left out the dill weed.

I followed the recipe for the most part. I didn't have dijon mustard so I used honey mustard and about 1/4 tsp. horseradish. It was a good call as it added a tiny bit of a bite. Next time I will do the same, but add only about 1/8 tsp. Also, I baked them instead of fry. The were nice and crunchy. I would definitely bake them again. Next time I may try adding a little bit of shredded cheese to the mix as well......
I used sweet potatoes instead of reg mashed potatoes substituted honey mustard instead of dijon . Baked them for a healthier recipe. Served with fresh string beans from garden .

I've had this recipe saved for a very long time. I had some leftover smoked ham and we've been eating too much soup lately, so - BINGO! Gotta try this, and I'm so glad I did. I didn't have any leftover mashed potatoes so I quickly whipped some up. Because the ham was smoked, I used Country Dijon mustard. I used my mini-chopper for the ham and green onions since I'd already sliced my finger 2 days before (ahem, never mind....) . The flavors blended perfectly. Even though I formed the patties and refrigerated for an hour, they were still a little loose, my fault, not the recipe's. One less pulse in the chopper should cure that next time :) Hubs came home late from a meeting so I left the pan out for him with instructions to reheat. The next morning he said, "What was that you made last night? They were REALLY good!" An absolute keeper that I'll definitely make again. I really want to try them for breakfast with a fried egg on top - oh YUM! Thank you, Avon, for a delicious and simple recipe using leftovers!!

I made this as written. It was good but not great. I will make it again. As empty nesters this made a lot - we ate half and have half left over. Next time I will cook them a bit longer as we liked the deeper brown, crunchy ones best. I will serve with a tossed salad and scrambled eggs

My just-made instant mashed potatoes were a bit runny so I had to add more panko crumbs and onions. Leftover cold-from-the-frig mashed potatoes would work best. I also added grated parmesan. Everyone enjoyed them with Cranberry chutney tonight and plan on leftovers with an over-easy fried egg for breakfast tomorrow!

Found a little dry and heavy. Next time will make with a mashed potato and acorn squash mixture for more creamy and less dense. Also, I used the George Forman grill instead of oil. Liked the outcome, but will crust the outside with cornmeal instead of Panko next time.
The thicker ones stayed together somewhat. Not to our taste. I will not make this again!
Absolutely delicious. They completely fell apart while cooking, even after adding extra breadcrumbs. But I don’t even care bc they are still so so tasty, I love it.
Very tasty. I didn't have green onion so just used finely chopped yellow onion. I also had leftover corn that I added. Came out great
OK but not as good as I hope

Great way of reusing the mashed potatoes when you have just a bit too much from the say before. Let's be honest, there are only that many days in a row you can eat them on the side!
I substituted ham with bacon, and also added some of the leftover cauliflower/ham gratin. The spring onions really elevate this dish! 
I served with homemade mustard/Dijon mustard/oat "cream" sauce and it was perfect. I served a slice of cured salmon with sour cream and dill sauce to complement this fresh snack.

I finely chopped some of our leftover ham from Easter dinner to use in this recipe. This recipe was easy to follow and prepare. My family really enjoyed these ham cakes and said the recipe was a keeper. We did serve it was some honey mustard and we also had applesauce as a side dish as others suggested. We will be making this again.
Mine were not as pretty, but the taste was wonderful
Easy and quick to make. Served with a honey mustard sauce!

had no dijon so I just used regular mustard...also was short on panko so I also used Italian bread crumbs....didn't use any salt as I thought the ham was salty enough on it's own....I will definitely use this recipe again ....Linda Wojick
P.S. hubby loved it too
